title: Review DOJ hiring practices for impartiality and compliance with law
uncertainties: The 2025-02-05 memorandum was re-read in full on justice.gov in review on 2026-10-18; it has no numbered sections, directs component reviews on pages 1 and 2 with a report to the Office of the Attorney General due 2025-03-15, asks for attention to race- or sex-based criteria rather than merit, and in footnote 3 asks components to consult the Office of Legal Counsel before acting against an existing legal obligation and to explain any directive not implemented. It does not mention hiring committees, ideology or political affiliation. Component reports were not found and may not be public, so whether the ordered reviews were completed is not verified. An earlier review search found reports of rescinded 2025 Honors Program offers and a 2026 memorandum suspending a one-year experience requirement for new prosecutors (reported by The Harvard Crimson), neither of which is a review of career hiring committees. The memorandum addresses DEI-related hiring, which overlaps only in part with the Mandate's concern about ideological hiring. The stage rests partly on the absence of a committee review, which was not run through a full systematic check.
